articles.title: Why PDF compression quietly turns your text into a picture
articles.excerpt: A 6-page text PDF went from 298.7 KB to 8.9 KB with every one of its 26,652 characters still selectable. The usual way to shrink a PDF gets to 30.5 KB and zero. There are two ways to make a PDF smalle…
articles.body: A 6-page text PDF went from 298.7 KB to 8.9 KB with every one of its 26,652 characters still selectable. The usual way to shrink a PDF gets to 30.5 KB and zero. There are two ways to make a PDF smaller. Only one of them keeps the document a document. The common way is to render every page to an image and rebuild the file from those images. It always works, it works on scanned documents, and it is what most compressors reach for when a file refuses to shrink. What it also does, quietly, is delete the text layer — the document still looks right on screen, but it is now a photograph of words. The other way is to leave the pages alone and shrink the file around them: collapse duplicated objects, and compress the streams that hold the actual content.

One of my projects is DocumentAI Analysis Platform , an AI powered platform that helps users analyze documents and find information quickly. The goal is simple: instead of manually reading long documents, users can upload files and ask questions in natural language. The platform supports PDF, Word, Excel, and scanned documents. articles.title: Sending text as images cut my Claude tokens by up to 81%. It also started inventing numbers.
articles.excerpt: There is a trick going around for cutting Claude Code bills: render bulky context (system prompt, tool docs, logs, old history) as dense PNG images instead of text. An image is billed by its pixel siz…
articles.body: There is a trick going around for cutting Claude Code bills: render bulky context (system prompt, tool docs, logs, old history) as dense PNG images instead of text. An image is billed by its pixel size, not by how much text is inside it, so a page packed with small characters can cost far fewer tokens than the same text. The open-source proxy pxpipe does exactly this and reports a 59-70% lower bill. Its own README is honest that the method is lossy. I wanted an independent number for both sides: how many tokens it really saves, and what the model can still read back.

articles.body: I'm building Underpeaks, a headless CMS that generates Flutter and Next.js apps from the same data models. It's in early testing, and most of what I've learned has come from things breaking. Here are four of those bugs, with what each one changed about how I build. 1. A UI flag that deleted the primary key Fields in a model can be marked hidden . I added that for the admin UI: hide a field from the editing form. Later I reused the same flag in the public API, so hidden fields would also be stripped from responses. One boolean, two meanings. The first generated Flutter app that used a model with a hidden field crashed with: type 'Null' is not a subtype of type 'String' The generated Dart model declares id as a non-nullable String .

articles.title: Previously resolved topics re-raised across sessions despite MEMORY.md
articles.excerpt: That is the title of an issue filed against Claude Code yesterday, on Windows, version 2.1.302. The reporter's own words, translated from Turkish: "It re-presented a topic that had been decided last n…
articles.body: That is the title of an issue filed against Claude Code yesterday, on Windows, version 2.1.302. The reporter's own words, translated from Turkish: "It re-presented a topic that had been decided last night as if we had never spoken about it today. And that is even though I told it MEMORY.md." It would be easy to file that under "the model forgot". I do not think that is what happened. Nothing was lost. The record was in the file. What was missing was any mechanism for saying that the topic was already closed. Four reports in about twenty-four hours I read the public issue streams for agent memory every week. This batch reads like four products failing in four different ways, until you notice they fail in only two.

articles.body: The first book in a new series called The Dell Chronicles, HL Bernabe’s Cooking Up Magick sets out to be a cozier fantasy version of The Lord of the Rings . And in many ways, it does pull directly from J.R.R. Tolkien’s world. The main character, Paisley, is a halfling who gets swept up on an adventure with a pair of dwarves, but unbeknownst to her, there’s also an evil overlord that has just returned after centuries – and she’s the only hope the world has to actually stop him. The similarities to The Hobbit and LOTR pretty much end there though, and you don’t get nearly enough detail in the first book to effectively flesh out this alternate version of Middle-earth. What you do get is a lovable main character who is surrounded by an interesting cast of characters.

articles.title: SpaceX will attempt 1st-ever double Starship rocket catch on next test launch, a 'profound technology milestone,' Elon Musk says
articles.excerpt: SpaceX will try to recover both Starship stages during the megarocket's next test flight, which is expected to take place in November, according to Elon Musk.
articles.body: SpaceX will soon notch a huge spaceflight milestone, if all goes according to plan. The company will try to catch both stages of its Starship megarocket during the vehicle's next test flight, which is targeted for next month, founder and CEO Elon Musk announced during SpaceX's quarter 3 (Q3) earnings call today (Oct. 20). If SpaceX succeeds, this "will be the first time that an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered," Musk said. "The only way that we can extend consciousness beyond Earth on a sustained basis is with a fully reusable orbital launch vehicle.

With this update, Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in can tap into your information across Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. As an example, Google says you can ask Gemini about your flight status if you're driving to the airport. The AI assistant can pull your flight details from a confirmation message in Gmail and then use that information to look up the status. articles.body: Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a possible merger, Elon Musk said during the latter's third quarter earnings call Tuesday . Musk, who serves as CEO of both companies, said the special committees were formed at the request of shareholders and consist of independent directors (though he did not name them). He also noted that he is not a member of either committee, nor involved in any of the discussions. "Because I'm a conflicted party, I can't actually be in the discussions of the special committees," Musk said.
